schema: CREATE CONSTRAINT vendor_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Vendor) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT employee_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Employee) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT account_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:BankAccount) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT change_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:BankChange) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT po_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:PurchaseOrder) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT grn_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:GoodsReceipt) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT invoice_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Invoice) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT payment_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Payment) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT bankline_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:BankLine) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT gstr_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:GstrLine) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE VECTOR INDEX grn_item IF NOT EXISTS FOR (g:GoodsReceipt) ON g.item_vec WITH [g.vendor_id]

checks.title: Invoice has no goods receipt
checks.plain: The vendor billed us against a purchase order that shows nothing received. Before chasing the vendor, look for a receipt keyed against the wrong PO.
checks.graph: Invoice -BILLS-> PurchaseOrder <-RECEIVED_AGAINST- (nothing). A vector search over receipt item text (same vendor) finds lookalike receipts; the graph then rejects any already received against another PO or with a different quantity.
checks.text:
// title: Invoice has no goods receipt
// plain: The vendor billed us against a purchase order that shows nothing received. Before chasing the vendor, look for a receipt keyed against the wrong PO.
// graph: Invoice -BILLS-> PurchaseOrder <-RECEIVED_AGAINST- (nothing). A vector search over receipt item text (same vendor) finds lookalike receipts; the graph then rejects any already received against another PO or with a different quantity.
MATCH (i:Invoice)-[:BILLS]->(po:PurchaseOrder)-[:PLACED_WITH]->(v:Vendor)
WHERE NOT EXISTS { (po)<-[:RECEIVED_AGAINST]-(:GoodsReceipt) }
OPTIONAL CALL (po) {
  MATCH (g:GoodsReceipt)
  SEARCH g IN (VECTOR INDEX grn_item FOR po.item_vec WHERE g.vendor_id = po.vendor_id LIMIT 5) SCORE AS sim
  OPTIONAL MATCH (g)-[:RECEIVED_AGAINST]->(other:PurchaseOrder)
  WITH g, sim, other
  ORDER BY sim DESC
  RETURN collect({id: g.id, sim: round(sim, 2), qty: g.qty, ref: g.po_ref, date: g.date, item: g.item, linked_to: other.id}) AS considered
}
WITH i, po, v, considered, [c IN considered WHERE c.linked_to IS NULL AND c.qty = po.qty] AS eligible
WITH i, po, v, considered, CASE WHEN size(eligible) > 0 THEN eligible[0] END AS candidate
WITH i, po, v, candidate, [c IN considered WHERE candidate IS NULL OR c.id <> candidate.id] AS rejected
RETURN 'missing-receipt' AS check,
       'medium' AS severity,
       i.id AS invoice,
       'No goods receipt for ' + po.id AS headline,
       i.id + ' bills ' + toString(po.qty) + ' x ' + po.item + ' on ' + po.id + ', but nothing has been received against that PO. ' +
       CASE WHEN candidate IS NULL THEN 'No unlinked receipt from this vendor looks like it.'
         ELSE candidate.id + ' ("' + candidate.item + '", ' + toString(candidate.qty) + ' received on ' + candidate.date +
              ') is from the same vendor, linked to no PO, and was keyed against ' + candidate.ref + ', a PO number that does not exist.' +
              reduce(s = '', r IN rejected | s + ' ' + r.id + ' looks closer (' + toString(r.sim) + ') but ' +
                     CASE WHEN r.linked_to IS NOT NULL THEN 'is already received against ' + r.linked_to + '.'
                          ELSE 'has a different quantity (' + toString(r.qty) + ').' END)
       END AS detail,
       i.total AS amount,
       [v.id, po.id, i.id] AS path,
       {after: po.id, label: 'GoodsReceipt', text: 'expected: a receipt against ' + po.id} AS missing,
       CASE WHEN candidate IS NULL THEN null
         ELSE {action: 'link_receipt', grn: candidate.id, po: po.id, similarity: candidate.sim,
               rejected: [r IN rejected | r.id + ' ' + toString(r.sim) + CASE WHEN r.linked_to IS NOT NULL THEN ', already on ' + r.linked_to ELSE ', qty ' + toString(r.qty) END],
               text: 'Link ' + candidate.id + ' to ' + po.id + ' (keyed as ' + candidate.ref + ')'}
       END AS suggestion

checks.title: Billed more than was received
checks.plain: Add up every receipt on the purchase order and every invoice billed against it. If the vendor billed more units than arrived, the difference was paid for nothing.
checks.graph: Many receipts and many invoices meet at one PurchaseOrder; both sides are summed across the fan-in. Duplicate invoices are left to check 4.
checks.text:
// title: Billed more than was received
// plain: Add up every receipt on the purchase order and every invoice billed against it. If the vendor billed more units than arrived, the difference was paid for nothing.
// graph: Many receipts and many invoices meet at one PurchaseOrder; both sides are summed across the fan-in. Duplicate invoices are left to check 4.
MATCH (po:PurchaseOrder)<-[:BILLS]-(i:Invoice)
WHERE NOT EXISTS {
  MATCH (po)<-[:BILLS]-(j:Invoice)
  WHERE j.id < i.id AND j.norm_no = i.norm_no AND j.vendor_id = i.vendor_id
}
WITH po, collect(i) AS invoices, sum(i.qty) AS billed
MATCH (g:GoodsReceipt)-[:RECEIVED_AGAINST]->(po)
WITH po, invoices, billed, collect(g) AS receipts, sum(g.qty) AS received
WHERE billed > received
UNWIND invoices AS i
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Payment)-[:SETTLES]->(i)
WITH po, i, billed, received, receipts, collect(p.id) AS payments
WITH po, i, billed, received, receipts, payments,
     toInteger(round((billed - received) * po.rate * 1.18)) AS excess
RETURN 'over-billed' AS check,
       CASE WHEN size(payments) > 0 THEN 'high' ELSE 'medium' END AS severity,
       i.id AS invoice,
       'Billed ' + toString(billed) + ', received ' + toString(received) AS headline,
       i.id + ' bills ' + toString(billed) + ' units on ' + po.id + '. ' + toString(size(receipts)) +
       ' receipts (' + reduce(s = '', g IN receipts | s + CASE WHEN s = '' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + g.id + ': ' + toString(g.qty)) +
       ') add up to ' + toString(received) + '. ' +
       CASE WHEN size(payments) > 0 THEN 'It was paid in full, so ' ELSE '' END +
       toString(billed - received) + ' units, Rs ' + toString(excess) + ' with GST, have no goods behind them.' AS detail,
       excess AS amount,
       [r IN receipts | r.id] + [po.id, i.id] + payments AS path,
       {after: po.id, label: 'GoodsReceipt', text: 'expected: ' + toString(billed - received) + ' more units received'} AS missing,
       null AS suggestion

checks.title: Payment came back from the bank
checks.plain: One payment can settle several invoices and leave the bank as several debits. If a debit is later returned, the books still say "paid" but the money never reached the vendor.
checks.graph: Invoice <-SETTLES- Payment <-CLEARS- BankLine, then a quantified path pattern follows any chain of REVERSES lines back. The shortfall is charged to the latest invoices first.
checks.text:
// title: Payment came back from the bank
// plain: One payment can settle several invoices and leave the bank as several debits. If a debit is later returned, the books still say "paid" but the money never reached the vendor.
// graph: Invoice <-SETTLES- Payment <-CLEARS- BankLine, then a quantified path pattern follows any chain of REVERSES lines back. The shortfall is charged to the latest invoices first.
MATCH (p:Payment)<-[:CLEARS]-(out:BankLine)
OPTIONAL MATCH (out)((:BankLine)<-[:REVERSES]-(:BankLine)){1,3}(back:BankLine)
WITH p, collect(DISTINCT out) AS debits, collect(DISTINCT back) AS returns
WITH p, debits, returns,
     reduce(s = 0, b IN debits | s + b.amount) - reduce(s = 0, b IN returns | s + b.amount) AS net
WHERE size(returns) > 0 AND net < p.amount
MATCH (p)-[a:SETTLES]->(i:Invoice)
WITH p, debits, returns, net, i, a ORDER BY i.date DESC
WITH p, debits, returns, net, collect({inv: i, amt: a.amount}) AS allocs
UNWIND range(0, size(allocs) - 1) AS k
WITH p, debits, returns, net, allocs, k,
     p.amount - net - reduce(s = 0, x IN allocs[0..k] | s + x.amt) AS left_before
WITH p, debits, returns, net, allocs, allocs[k].inv AS i,
     CASE WHEN left_before <= 0 THEN 0
          WHEN left_before >= allocs[k].amt THEN allocs[k].amt
          ELSE left_before END AS unpaid
WHERE unpaid > 0
RETURN 'payment-returned' AS check,
       'high' AS severity,
       i.id AS invoice,
       'Marked paid, Rs ' + toString(unpaid) + ' came back' AS headline,
       p.id + ' settles ' + toString(size(allocs)) + ' invoices for Rs ' + toString(p.amount) + '. It left the bank as ' +
       toString(size(debits)) + ' debits; ' + reduce(s = '', b IN returns | s + b.id + ' (' + b.date + ', Rs ' + toString(b.amount) + ') ') +
       'returned the money: "' + returns[0].narration + '". Only Rs ' + toString(net) + ' actually left. ' +
       i.id + ' is the latest invoice on the payment, so Rs ' + toString(unpaid) + ' of it is still owed.' AS detail,
       unpaid AS amount,
       [i.id, p.id] + [b IN debits | b.id] + [b IN returns | b.id] AS path,
       null AS missing,
       null AS suggestion

checks.title: Same invoice paid twice
checks.plain: The vendor's invoice number was keyed twice in slightly different forms (BOS/889 and BOS-889). Both copies were approved and both were paid.
checks.graph: Two Invoice nodes share a Vendor, a normalised invoice number, an amount and a PurchaseOrder; each has its own Payment and BankLine.
checks.text:
// title: Same invoice paid twice
// plain: The vendor's invoice number was keyed twice in slightly different forms (BOS/889 and BOS-889). Both copies were approved and both were paid.
// graph: Two Invoice nodes share a Vendor, a normalised invoice number, an amount and a PurchaseOrder; each has its own Payment and BankLine.
MATCH (a:Invoice)-[:ISSUED_BY]->(v:Vendor)<-[:ISSUED_BY]-(b:Invoice)
WHERE a.id < b.id AND a.norm_no = b.norm_no AND a.total = b.total
OPTIONAL MATCH (b)-[:BILLS]->(po:PurchaseOrder)<-[:BILLS]-(a)
OPTIONAL MATCH (pa:Payment)-[:SETTLES]->(a)
OPTIONAL MATCH (pb:Payment)-[:SETTLES]->(b)
OPTIONAL MATCH (la:BankLine)-[:CLEARS]->(pa)
OPTIONAL MATCH (lb:BankLine)-[:CLEARS]->(pb)
WITH a, b, v, po, collect(DISTINCT pa) AS pas, collect(DISTINCT pb) AS pbs, collect(DISTINCT la) AS las, collect(DISTINCT lb) AS lbs
RETURN 'duplicate-invoice' AS check,
       CASE WHEN size(pas) > 0 AND size(pbs) > 0 THEN 'high' ELSE 'medium' END AS severity,
       b.id AS invoice,
       'Duplicate of ' + a.id + CASE WHEN size(pas) > 0 AND size(pbs) > 0 THEN ', both paid' ELSE '' END AS headline,
       b.id + ' (' + b.vendor_inv_no + ', ' + b.date + ') and ' + a.id + ' (' + a.vendor_inv_no + ', ' + a.date + ') are the same ' +
       v.name + ' invoice for Rs ' + toString(a.total) +
       CASE WHEN po IS NULL THEN '' ELSE ' against ' + po.id END + '. ' +
       CASE WHEN size(pas) > 0 AND size(pbs) > 0
         THEN 'It was paid twice: ' + pas[0].id + CASE WHEN size(las) > 0 THEN ' (' + las[0].id + ')' ELSE '' END + ' and ' + pbs[0].id + CASE WHEN size(lbs) > 0 THEN ' (' + lbs[0].id + ')' ELSE '' END + '. Recover Rs ' + toString(b.total) + ' from the vendor.'
         ELSE 'Block the second copy before it is paid.' END AS detail,
       CASE WHEN size(pbs) > 0 THEN b.total ELSE 0 END AS amount,
       [a.id] + [p IN pas | p.id] + [l IN las | l.id] + CASE WHEN po IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [po.id] END + [b.id] + [p IN pbs | p.id] + [l IN lbs | l.id] AS path,
       null AS missing,
       null AS suggestion

checks.title: Tax credit claimed, supplier never filed
checks.plain: We claimed the GST input credit on this invoice, but it is missing from our GSTR-2B because the supplier never reported it in their GSTR-1, so the credit can be reversed with interest.
checks.graph: Invoice {itc_claimed: true} with no incoming REPORTS from a GstrLine, while the same supplier's other invoices are reported - so it is this invoice, not the supplier, that is missing.
checks.text:
// title: Tax credit claimed, supplier never filed
// plain: We claimed the GST input credit on this invoice, but it is missing from our GSTR-2B because the supplier never reported it in their GSTR-1, so the credit can be reversed with interest.
// graph: Invoice {itc_claimed: true} with no incoming REPORTS from a GstrLine, while the same supplier's other invoices are reported - so it is this invoice, not the supplier, that is missing.
MATCH (i:Invoice {itc_claimed: true})-[:ISSUED_BY]->(v:Vendor)
WHERE NOT EXISTS { (:GstrLine)-[:REPORTS]->(i) }
OPTIONAL MATCH (other:GstrLine)-[:REPORTS]->(:Invoice)-[:ISSUED_BY]->(v)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Payment)-[:SETTLES]->(i)
WITH i, v, collect(DISTINCT other) AS filed, collect(DISTINCT p.id) AS payments
RETURN 'gst-not-filed' AS check,
       'medium' AS severity,
       i.id AS invoice,
       'GST credit Rs ' + toString(i.gst) + ' at risk' AS headline,
       'We claimed Rs ' + toString(i.gst) + ' input tax credit on ' + i.id + ' (' + v.name + ' ' + i.vendor_inv_no + ', ' + i.date +
       '), but it is missing from our GSTR-2B: the supplier never reported it in their GSTR-1. ' +
       CASE WHEN size(filed) > 0 THEN 'They did report ' + toString(size(filed)) + CASE WHEN size(filed) = 1 THEN ' other invoice' ELSE ' other invoices' END + ' to us, so this one was skipped. '
            ELSE 'They have not reported any invoice to us. ' END +
       CASE WHEN size(payments) > 0 THEN 'The invoice is already paid (' + payments[0] + '), so ask the supplier to file or hold the credit.'
            ELSE 'Hold the payment until they file.' END AS detail,
       i.gst AS amount,
       [v.id, i.id] + payments AS path,
       {after: i.id, label: 'GstrLine', text: 'expected: ' + i.vendor_inv_no + ' in our GSTR-2B'} AS missing,
       null AS suggestion

checks.title: Large payment to a just-changed bank account
checks.plain: The vendor's bank details changed shortly before a large payment. Then follow every short path from that payment to our own people: who approved it, who entered the new account, who owns it.
checks.graph: Payment -PAID_TO-> BankAccount <-HAS_ACCOUNT {since}- Vendor, then a quantified path pattern of 1-3 hops over PAID_TO|HAS_ACCOUNT|NEW_ACCOUNT|ENTERED|APPROVED from the Payment to any Employee.
checks.text:
// title: Large payment to a just-changed bank account
// plain: The vendor's bank details changed shortly before a large payment. Then follow every short path from that payment to our own people: who approved it, who entered the new account, who owns it.
// graph: Payment -PAID_TO-> BankAccount <-HAS_ACCOUNT {since}- Vendor, then a quantified path pattern of 1-3 hops over PAID_TO|HAS_ACCOUNT|NEW_ACCOUNT|ENTERED|APPROVED from the Payment to any Employee.
MATCH (i:Invoice)<-[:SETTLES]-(p:Payment)-[:PAID_TO]->(ba:BankAccount)<-[h:HAS_ACCOUNT]-(v:Vendor)
WHERE p.amount >= 500000 AND duration.inDays(date(h.since), date(p.date)).days <= 14
OPTIONAL MATCH (c:BankChange)-[:NEW_ACCOUNT]->(ba)
OPTIONAL MATCH path = (p)((x)-[:PAID_TO|HAS_ACCOUNT|NEW_ACCOUNT|ENTERED|APPROVED]-(y)){1,3}(e:Employee)
WITH i, p, ba, h, v, c, e, collect(DISTINCT [r IN relationships(path) | type(r)]) AS routes
WITH i, p, ba, h, v, c, e, routes,
     CASE WHEN any(rt IN routes WHERE rt = ['PAID_TO', 'HAS_ACCOUNT']) THEN 'owns the receiving account' END AS owns,
     CASE WHEN any(rt IN routes WHERE rt = ['APPROVED']) THEN 'approved the payment' END AS approved,
     CASE WHEN any(rt IN routes WHERE rt = ['PAID_TO', 'NEW_ACCOUNT', 'ENTERED']) THEN 'entered the new bank details' END AS entered,
     CASE WHEN any(rt IN routes WHERE rt = ['PAID_TO', 'NEW_ACCOUNT', 'APPROVED']) THEN 'approved the bank change' END AS ok_change
WITH i, p, ba, h, v, c,
     collect(CASE WHEN e IS NULL THEN null ELSE {id: e.id, name: e.name, role: e.role,
                  roles: [x IN [owns, approved, entered, ok_change] WHERE x IS NOT NULL]} END) AS people
WITH i, p, ba, h, v, c, people, [x IN people WHERE 'owns the receiving account' IN x.roles] AS owners
RETURN 'new-bank-account' AS check,
       CASE WHEN size(owners) > 0 THEN 'high' ELSE 'medium' END AS severity,
       i.id AS invoice,
       CASE WHEN size(owners) > 0 THEN 'Paid to an employee\'s account' ELSE 'Paid to a bank account added ' +
            toString(duration.inDays(date(h.since), date(p.date)).days) + ' days earlier' END AS headline,
       p.id + ' paid Rs ' + toString(p.amount) + ' to account ' + ba.id + ' on ' + p.date + '. ' + v.name + ' switched to that account on ' +
       h.since + ', ' + toString(duration.inDays(date(h.since), date(p.date)).days) + ' days earlier' +
       CASE WHEN c IS NULL THEN '. ' ELSE ' (' + c.id + ': "' + c.reason + '"). ' END +
       reduce(s = '', x IN people | s + x.name + ' (' + x.role + ') ' +
              reduce(t = '', r IN x.roles | t + CASE WHEN t = '' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + r) + '. ') AS detail,
       p.amount AS amount,
       [i.id, p.id, ba.id] + CASE WHEN c IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [c.id] END + [x IN people | x.id] + [v.id] AS path,
       null AS missing,
       null AS suggestion

trail.title: The trail of one invoice
trail.plain: Everything an accountant would pull to tie out one invoice: the vendor, the PO, every receipt on it, every payment and the other invoices it covers, every bank line, returns, the GSTR-2B line, and where the money went.
trail.graph: A quantified path pattern of 0-3 hops over the document links, which never walks through another invoice or a bank account (so a vendor's other work stays out), plus any extra nodes a finding points at ($extra).
trail.text:
// title: The trail of one invoice
// plain: Everything an accountant would pull to tie out one invoice: the vendor, the PO, every receipt on it, every payment and the other invoices it covers, every bank line, returns, the GSTR-2B line, and where the money went.
// graph: A quantified path pattern of 0-3 hops over the document links, which never walks through another invoice or a bank account (so a vendor's other work stays out), plus any extra nodes a finding points at ($extra).
MATCH (i:Invoice {id: $id})-[:ISSUED_BY]->(v:Vendor)
MATCH p = (i)(()-[:BILLS|RECEIVED_AGAINST|SETTLES|CLEARS|REVERSES|REPORTS|PAID_TO]-()){0,3}(n)
WHERE none(x IN nodes(p)[1..-1] WHERE x:Invoice OR x:BankAccount)
WITH v, collect(DISTINCT n) AS walked
OPTIONAL MATCH (x) WHERE x.id IN $extra
WITH walked, v, collect(DISTINCT x) AS pointed
UNWIND walked + [v] + pointed AS a
WITH collect(DISTINCT a) AS ns
UNWIND ns AS a
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) WHERE b IN ns
WITH ns, collect(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r IS NULL THEN null ELSE {from: a.id, to: b.id, type: type(r), props: properties(r)} END) AS rels
RETURN [n IN ns | {id: n.id, label: labels(n)[0], props: properties(n)}] AS nodes, rels

link_receipt.title: Link a goods receipt to the PO it belongs to
link_receipt.plain: The one write Trailmark makes. It only links a receipt that is linked to nothing, to a PO from the same vendor, and it records who linked it, why, and what the receipt was keyed as.
